R6, FB top. SOURCING SUBSTITUTION FROM ARCHITECTURE, FLAGGED: sheets.md/blocks.md name '~116k' (e.g. 116k/22.1k, ratio 6.249) but 116k is NOT a standard E96 value and has ZERO stock in any 0603 SMD tolerance at LCSC live (only obsolete/zero-stock THT precision parts exist under that code). Substituted 115k, the nearest E96 0.1% value with real 0603 SMD stock (28790 pcs). This is independently corroborated, not just a stock-driven guess: the AP64350 datasheet's own Typical Application Circuit (Fig.1, VOUT=5V row) specifies R1=115k / R2=22.1k for exactly this output voltage - i.e. the IC vendor's own reference design uses 115k, not 116k. RE-CHECKED SIM-1 (decisions.md): with R6=115k/R7=22.1k, Vout across Vref 792-808mV and +/-0.1% resistor tolerance ranges 4.905V-5.021V - PASSES the 4.90-5.10V window but with only ~5mV of margin at the LOW corner (vs a wider margin using the vendor's own 116k figure, which nets ~4.999V nominal). A 118k substitute was checked and REJECTED: it fails the HIGH corner at 5.130V, over the 5.10V ceiling. P4/schematic phase should re-run SIM-1 with this exact substituted value before committing - the low-corner margin is thin enough to be worth a second look, not because 115k is wrong, but because the margin is real and small.
